analysis.title: Tech selloff highlights rising scrutiny of AI spending (UBS House View - Daily Asia)
key_insights: US tech led the market lower on Friday as AI buildout concerns overshadowed strong 3Q earnings. Nasdaq Composite fell 2.9% on the day and 2.0% on the week. S&P 500 fell 1.8% on the day and 0.6% on the week.

UBS says AI infrastructure demand remains exceptionally strong, but investors are weighting three concerns more heavily: overinvestment, financing and cannibalization. Earnings expectations were broadly met.

Overinvestment: Alphabet kept its USD 195-205bn 2026 capex plan, reported negative free cash flow for the quarter and signaled a significant further capex increase for 2027. Meta raised the low end of its 2026 capex range to USD 135-145bn and pledged continued aggressive investment beyond this year. Meta shares fell nearly 7% the next day on the higher capex floor and negative 3Q free cash flow.

Cloud growth, the key return-on-AI metric, is accelerating. Google Cloud revenue rose 103% y/y vs 82% in the prior quarter and 34% in the March quarter. Azure grew 48% vs 43% in the June quarter. Oracle growth rose to 62% from 47%. All three guided to further cloud growth.
Microsoft reported an eight-fold increase in large Copilot accounts. Alphabet said Gemini reached 1 billion users.

Financing: neocloud credit has sold off on a maturity and funding mismatch. Large upfront debt-financed investment is backed by later cash flows that depend on utilisation, execution, customer renewal and refinancing conditions.

Neoclouds are about 8% of UBS's capex estimate vs about 80% for Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and SpaceX. UBS expects selective project delays, repricing and consolidation rather than a broad collapse in AI spending.
Cannibalization: Alphabet Search query growth hit a five-year high but Search revenue growth slowed, with management saying AI Mode monetizes at a lower rate.

Intel shares fell 28.6% on Friday. AI is boosting server orders but also causing component scarcity, so Intel cannot fully meet data center demand. Scarcity is raising PC prices, which hurts its client business.
UBS raised aggregate AI capex forecasts to USD 1.0tr for 2026 and USD 1.4tr for 2027, and introduced USD 1.5tr for 2028.
UBS expects higher volatility in the AI trade to be the new normal. It does not think investors should abandon the AI theme.
UBS would worry about a sustained turn in AI investment if AI lab revenue growth slows meaningfully, cloud utilization weakens, or falling AI costs fail to stimulate enough new usage.

UBS would also reassess its outlook if algorithmic efficiency sharply cuts compute needs, if larger investments stop improving AI capabilities, or if tighter financial conditions limit hyperscaler funding.

Positioning advice: reduce overconcentration across the AI value chain, preferring foundry, compute and power names. Rebalance across sectors and asset classes. Prefer industrials, health care and financials, plus Eurozone, EM and Asia ex-Japan. Quality bonds rallied during the selloff. Use volatility deliberately (rebalance, hedge, generate income, or build exposure at predefined prices).

Asia sentiment was fragile into Monday: Nikkei 225 and Kospi both opened down more than 1%. Brent reached USD 118/bbl on Friday on fears the US may resume strikes on Iran, then eased to about USD 111/bbl in early Monday trade.

market_movers.rationale: Shares fell nearly 7% the day after 3Q results as investors focused on the higher capex floor (USD 135-145bn for 2026) and negative free cash flow.
Shares fell 28.6% on Friday. AI server demand is colliding with component scarcity, which limits data center supply and raises PC prices that hurt the client business.
Negative 3Q free cash flow, a signaled further capex rise in 2027 and slower Search revenue growth, offset by Google Cloud revenue up 103% y/y.

earnings_insights: Alphabet 3Q (reported): Google Cloud revenue +103% y/y vs +82% in 2Q and +34% in the March quarter. Free cash flow negative for the quarter. 2026 capex plan kept at USD 195-205bn, with a significant further increase signaled for 2027. Search query growth at a five-year high, Search revenue growth decelerated.
Alphabet shares fell almost 13% the day after results (the report text is truncated before the company name, but the context is the Alphabet overinvestment paragraph).
Meta 3Q (reported): 2026 capex range low end raised to USD 135-145bn, with aggressive investment pledged beyond 2026. Free cash flow negative for the quarter. Shares fell nearly 7% the next day.
Microsoft (reported, quarter to September): Azure grew 48% vs 43% for the June quarter. Large Copilot accounts increased eight-fold.
Oracle (reported): cloud growth accelerated to 62% from 47%.
Intel (reported): shares fell 28.6% on Friday. Server orders up on AI but data center demand not fully met due to component scarcity.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Fell 1bp on Friday and 7bps on the week as quality bonds rallied during the equity selloff.
Rose on concerns the US may resume military strikes against Iran, then reversed in early Monday trade.
Listed under 'What to watch' for the session. No figure given.
Raised on stronger spending commitments from the largest hyperscalers.

risk_factors: AI lab revenue growth slowing meaningfully.
Falling AI costs failing to stimulate enough new usage to absorb expanding capacity.
Algorithmic efficiency gains sharply reducing compute requirements.
Larger investments failing to deliver commensurate gains in AI capabilities.
Tighter financial conditions limiting hyperscaler funding of new investment.
Neocloud maturity and funding mismatch, with sensitivity to utilisation, execution, renewals and refinancing.
Possible resumption of US military strikes against Iran, which would lift oil.
vol_and_positioning: UBS expects higher volatility in the AI trade to be the new normal at this stage of the cycle.

Investors should prepare for further volatility and decide in advance how to respond. Swings can be used to rebalance, manage downside risk, generate income or build exposure gradually at predefined prices.
Structured strategies carry issuer, liquidity, pricing and capital-loss risks and should be sized to risk tolerance.
Single-stock risk is elevated this earnings season. UBS advises reducing overconcentration across the AI value chain.
geopolitical: Concerns that the US may resume military strikes against Iran pushed Brent to USD 118/bbl on Friday before it eased to about USD 111/bbl in early Monday trade.
